claims.claim: A-4 excludes KBV/KBA from identity verification while permitting KBV in fraud management.
claims.evidenceLimit: Purpose matters; no worldwide prohibition on every knowledge question.
claims.proposedMeaning: Do not count supplemental screening as this revision’s verification method.

claims.claim: GAO identified breached personal data as material attackers could use to answer KBV questions.
claims.evidenceLimit: Historical federal study; no Proof/RON exploit or failure rate measured.
claims.proposedMeaning: Knowledge can be available to someone other than its subject.

claims.claim: LexisNexis describes proprietary linking, non-credit content, commercial/regulated sources and optional shared-secret/customer questions.
claims.evidenceLimit: Optional question types are not for new account/benefits enrollment. No Proof supplier linkage established; proprietary is not synonymous with publicly searchable.
claims.proposedMeaning: Identify engine and source categories before generalizing.

claims.claim: Proof describes third-party questions from credit history and public records, generally needing six months of U.S. credit history.
claims.evidenceLimit: Supplier, exact data mix and accuracy not established.
claims.proposedMeaning: Attribute credit-history wording to this product; do not infer a credit score, hard inquiry or ordinary credit report.

claims.claim: Proof says valid SSN/ITIN holders may get no questions because records are sparse or available questions exhausted.
claims.evidenceLimit: No population failure percentage or nationality rule supplied.
claims.proposedMeaning: Separate no questions from wrong answers and fraud.

claims.claim: Proof documents 4/5 in two minutes, immediate first retry, then 24/48-hour waits from first attempt, and no manual support unlock.
claims.evidenceLimit: Published instructions, not tested behavior or every state’s retry law.
claims.proposedMeaning: Notify sender and confirm route before more attempts.

claims.claim: Repeated attempts may expose more of a finite question pool; documented limits constrain attempts.
claims.evidenceLimit: No observed repetition, answer feedback, attack success or unlimited retry demonstrated.
claims.proposedMeaning: Retain bounded risk without claiming a proven easy bypass.

claims.claim: Proof’s general failure guide says any wrong answer fails; its dedicated KBA guide says 4/5 passes.
claims.evidenceLimit: Help-text conflict does not identify actual scoring behavior.
claims.proposedMeaning: Use dedicated threshold as attributed guidance and seek reconciliation.

claims.claim: Proof’s eligible no-SSN/no-ITIN route uses ID/selfie photos and requires a current or previous U.S. address.
claims.evidenceLimit: Conditional eligibility; no never-U.S.-address route established.
claims.proposedMeaning: No SSN does not mean no U.S.-footprint condition.

claims.claim: Proof’s overview makes methods depend on product/settings/notary state; KBA troubleshooting points to in-person fallback.
claims.evidenceLimit: An alternative may not be enabled on an existing invitation.
claims.proposedMeaning: Eligible alternative is a different route, not a manual unlock promise.

claims.claim: Proof lists foreign MRZ passports for online notarization.
claims.evidenceLimit: ID support alone establishes neither quiz generation nor second statutory method.
claims.proposedMeaning: Separate supported credential from completed verification.

claims.claim: Virginia’s 2021 Chapter 78 had personal knowledge, credible witness or at least two of four listed methods; no express KBA item.
claims.evidenceLimit: Do not use this list for older acts or assume separately adopted authorization without its source.
claims.proposedMeaning: Use transaction-date law and preserve existing ledger.

claims.claim: Chapter 832 added KBA as item (5), effective July 1, 2024 under the ordinary constitutional rule; its retrospective clause names §47.1-20.1(B).
claims.evidenceLimit: Textual timeline, not a decision invalidating earlier acts.
claims.proposedMeaning: Separate KBA insertion from validation arguments.

claims.claim: Current Virginia permits personal knowledge, qualifying credible witness or at least two listed methods, with KBA an option in that route.
claims.evidenceLimit: Permitted combinations need not be available in every product.
claims.proposedMeaning: Permission proves neither best practice, NIST conformity nor execution.

claims.claim: The certificate/PIV item names a valid digital certificate accessed by biometrics or qualifying PIV, not standalone selfie.
claims.evidenceLimit: No particular Proof signer credential/access evidence obtained.
claims.proposedMeaning: Ask for actual second method; distinguish signer and notary certificates.

claims.claim: The Virginia-listed method completing a particular Proof no-KBA session is not established here.
claims.evidenceLimit: Screenshots and IAL2 labels do not supply statutory mapping.
claims.proposedMeaning: Require dated authority and completed method results.

claims.claim: Virginia §47.1-14 requires care and a notarial record; the video/audio route requires recording and other-identification notation.
claims.evidenceLimit: Statutory minimum fields differ from additional recommended evidence.
claims.proposedMeaning: Retain lawful protected records; publish no identity records or quiz answers.

claims.claim: §47.1-20.1(B) limits invalidation solely for notary duty failures, preserves challenges/remedies and excludes unauthorized actors.
claims.evidenceLimit: No transaction validity determination.
claims.proposedMeaning: A method concern is neither automatic voidness nor compliance clearance.

claims.claim: A recipient’s approved-platform requirement may remain a practical barrier when another lawful route exists.
claims.evidenceLimit: No recipient-specific requirement or rejection obtained.
claims.proposedMeaning: Seek written document/output acceptance; promise no platform switch.

claims.claim: Proof Verify is an organization-enabled agent-verification product; its report/recording does not itself prove a notarial act.
claims.evidenceLimit: No live session or account inspected.
claims.proposedMeaning: Do not substitute agent verification for notarization automatically.

claims.claim: Notary Geek publicly describes eligible outside-U.S. passport intake without SSN/ITIN/KBA, with document/location/destination review.
claims.evidenceLimit: Public descriptions checked; no live acceptance, timing, price or result tested.
claims.proposedMeaning: Use maintained intake/support and confirm route before commitment.

claims.claim: Retain public/proprietary-record terminology with Proof’s explicit credit-history wording as a product-specific qualification.
claims.evidenceLimit: No supplier contract or independent FCRA classification examined. LexisNexis’s own product disclaimer is not Proof’s classification.
claims.proposedMeaning: Do not infer source mix or legal duties from absence of visible consent/freeze friction.

claims.claim: KBA replacements also need assessment of evidence, spoofing resistance, access barriers and redress.
claims.evidenceLimit: No head-to-head RON experiment performed.
claims.proposedMeaning: Do not label every biometric implementation superior or accessible.

claims.claim: Proof says each available question is used once per person; Virginia permits up to 60% initial-question reuse on additional quizzes.
claims.evidenceLimit: Different policy statements; no observed repetition or provider breach of statutory ceiling established.
claims.proposedMeaning: A permissible reuse maximum is not observed provider recycling.

measuredFacts.note: Published quiz parameters and documentation observations are not effectiveness measurements.

sourceRefreshLimits: Original notary.cx HTML/JSON endpoints were inaccessible through retrieval; authored explanations were read at corresponding notarygeek.net paths.
2026 Chapters 364/365 links returned JavaScript shells. Current Code was read directly; no complete 2026 amendment comparison claimed.
Chapter 832 plain endpoint initially returned database unavailable; +pdf= returned enacted text. No full forensic capture claimed.
No dated adopted §2.2-436 authority for the specific no-KBA flow was established. Missing mapping evidence does not establish no such authority exists.
Mutable sources require refresh before customer publication; displayed update times are provider metadata, not proven version histories.

contraryInterpretations.argument: Dynamic proprietary questions, limits and additional checks can be useful layered fraud controls.
contraryInterpretations.concession: Yes; data may be difficult to obtain and NIST permits fraud-management KBV.
contraryInterpretations.response: This does not establish A-4 identity verification or measured product effectiveness.

contraryInterpretations.argument: A properly performed Virginia KBA combination can be lawful despite NIST.
contraryInterpretations.concession: Yes; statutory permission and technical assurance answer different questions.
contraryInterpretations.response: Require dated combination, care and records; permission does not rank methods.

contraryInterpretations.argument: Proof has no-SSN, personal-knowledge, witness and agent options, so foreign signers are not universally excluded.
contraryInterpretations.response: Eligibility, address condition, enablement, statutory mapping and recipient acceptance remain specific.

contraryInterpretations.argument: Validation law can preserve an act despite a duty defect.
contraryInterpretations.concession: Material counter-law, not a cosmetic caveat.
contraryInterpretations.response: No validity/remedies ruling; preservation of an act and proof of compliance differ.
